correctness.rationale: The four-state de Bruijn graph is reconstructed from all eight Rule-54 triples. Exhaustive multiplication closure yields precisely 109 Boolean relations (77 admitting a loop, 31 acyclic, one with cycles but no loop). The unique exceptional relation is R_1 and has sole incoming right-product edge I --1--> R_1, with no incoming edge to I, so only the length-one word 1 can realize it. A finite four-vertex directed graph has a directed cycle iff some cycle of length at most four exists, making these checks exhaustive. For n>=2 every periodic image word yields a loop and hence an n-periodic input; shift equivariance gives the converse. Fixed inputs both map to zero and the alternating input maps to all ones. The standard-library checker closes the full finite state spaces and separately corroborates ring lengths 1–12; no finite sample is mistaken for an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Spatial periodic-point lifting is an intrinsic dynamical invariant for an important non-surjective classical CA. This is an exact global statement for every spatial period >=2, sharply isolating the sole fixed-point obstruction and specifying its minimal doubling remedy. It distinguishes relative surjectivity on image periodic points from full-shift surjectivity and from generic period-multiplier bounds; the result is more than an arbitrary finite-catalogue entry, despite using an exhaustive finite algebraic proof.
